title: The delivery-attempt log records one row per surfaced notification with the operator-readable fields for later inspection
asA: operator inspecting the notification behaviour of a shipped rcf-lite application
iWant: one row in the delivery-attempt log per notification the shell surfaced, with the priority, the category and the delivery and acknowledgement timestamps
soThat: I can reconcile what the shell said with what my operators saw and acknowledged

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a shipped surface that has surfaced N notifications, `GET /api/delivery-log` returns HTTP 200 with body `{ rows: [...] }` and `rows.length === N`; each row carries `notificationId` (string), `category` (string), `priority` (`"info"` or `"error"`), `deliveredAt` (ISO-8601 timestamp); a row for a dismissed toast additionally carries `dismissedAt`; a row for an acknowledged centre item additionally carries `acknowledgedAt`. Rows are append-only; a `notificationId` never appears twice on the same page load. The pack does not itself enumerate every row (the delivery log's persistence is delegated to the applied `logging` companion); the AC is a mechanism-reach gap for a v1.1 minor bump when the pack gains a log-shape probe.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a shipped surface after N notifications
acceptanceCriteria.then: N rows with the operator-readable fields are returned

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the delivery-log write factory (TAC-2102 `writeDeliveryRow`), a call from the toast factory and a call from the centre factory both write through the applied `logging` companion's record factory (the row shape lives on this blueprint; the persistence layer lives on the companion). A row written outside the companion's factory bypasses the companion's retention and audit path and is refused at project-side review.
acceptanceCriteria.when: a toast or centre event surfaces a notification
acceptanceCriteria.then: a row lands through the applied logging companion
